page.layout: One column of verse below a decorative ornament and a centred title (three lines); no running head; page number at head; no notes in the margins, only stray marks on the right edge.

main_text.head: IN IESVITAM COR REGIS HENRICI IV. petentem.
main_text.p: Quem nõ mille manus, nõ mille pericula mortis Quem nec & infidiis sternere quiuit Iber, Quem nequit Mars ipse ferox, fera sica peremit, Sica HENRICORVM sanguinolenta nece. Scilicet occubuit scelerata fraude petitus Arte, dolo, insidiis Rex, IVDAITA, tuis.

p.i: Quid sceleris latuit tanti sub corde Monarchae,
Sedibus eximiis te, & rursum in honore locauit,
Et plus quam par est, & ipse maiora tulisti,
Gratia pro meritis haec referenda fuit?

main_text.p: Vt cumulo adiiceret proprio te CORDE beauit, Quid maius proprio quis dare CORDE potest? Nunc cape COR toties a te mucrone petitum, HARLAEVS votis annuit ipse tuis.
Sed pariter cum DENTE, COR vt referatur eodem, Non sunt diuersis contumulanda locis Quae Natura simul iunxit, quae Parca reuulsit, Vsa instrumentis pestis amara tuis.

page.notes: Stray marks in the margins (a small asterisk after "nece", a numeral 1 at the right edge beside "mucrone", small dashes near "honore" and "referenda") are not clearly printed reference marks and are left out. "infidiis" is read as printed; the first letter could be an f or an i. The stains and show-through at the foot are not transcribed.
